paragraphs.text: Guardrails for DeepSeek Harness subagents: sandbox cap, destructive-command deny list, tool-surface
restriction, and cold-resume recovery.
# dsh-subagent-guard
Three gates for subagents in [DeepSeek Harness][dsh]: a **sandbox ceiling**, a **destructive-command
denylist**, and a **delegation tool** that pins each child's tool surface and system prompt.
> 中文说明见 README.zh-CN.md。
## The gap

When DSH creates a subagent it captures a **snapshot** of the parent session's policy
(`captureDeleg
atedPolicyOverrides` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent`):

- the child's approval policy is pinned to `never` — anything requiring approval is
rejected inside

the child, never escalated to a human;
- the child inherits the parent's **explicit** sandbox overri
side can widen it again.

This is a [deliberate design decision][note], not a bug: *"Snapshot-at-delegation is the
semantic: t

he child keeps the policy it was handed."* The consequence is that a
subagent gets exactly the privi

leges the parent handed over at spawn time, while having
none of the parent's context, history, or j

parent handed over at spawn time, while having
none of the parent's context, history, or judgement.

This plugin adds an operator-controlled ceiling on top of that snapshot — something the
harness inte
ntionally does not provide.
## Three gates
### Gate 1 — sandbox ceiling (`agent/created`)

On subagent creation the plugin reads the effective sandbox mode (session override or
deployment def

ault) and, if it is wider than `subagentSandboxCap`, appends a
`sandbox/mode` event lowering it. **D

owngrade only**: a `read-only` child is never
raised to `workspace-write`.

The mode is read **when `agent/created` fires**, not inside the plugin's `apply()`.
Through 0.4.2 th

e service snapshot was taken in `apply()` — where the service is usually
not registered yet (a real-

host probe measured every relevant service as `undefined` in
`apply`, becoming visible ~300 ms later

). The snapshot was therefore always empty, the
fail-closed branch always won, and a **narrower** ch

ild was raised to the cap. 0.4.3
reads the service inside the event.

If the mode still **cannot be read** at event time, the child is forced to
`subagentSandboxCap` and

an error is logged (fail-closed). This matters because gate 1 is
often the only thing standing betwe
en a subagent and `danger-full-access`.
Applies to subagents created *after* the plugin loads.
### Gate 2 — command denylist (`ctx.tools.guard`)

`ctx.tools.guard()` is a **monotonic gate**: it runs after the `tools/pre-execute`
waterfall and *ca

nnot be overridden in the allow direction* by any other plugin. A
returned string denies the call; t

here is no `ask` path around it and no approval
policy (`never` included) can bypass it.

Which tools does it inspect? **Any tool whose arguments carry a command string**, keyed
by `commandA

rg` (default `command`). This is deliberately *not* a tool-name allowlist —
an earlier version enume

rated `shellTools: [bash, pwsh]` and silently skipped every
third-party shell (e.g. `win_bash`) that

registered under a different name. Tool names
change per deployment; argument shape does not.
Default rules cover operations that cannot be undone without external media:
| Category | Examples |
| Shadow copies | `vssadmin delete shadows`, `wmic shadowcopy delete`, `Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCo

py … Delete` |
| Restore points | `Remove-ComputerRestorePoint`, `Disable-ComputerRestore` |
| Disks
/ partitions | `diskpart`, `Format-Volume`, `Clear-Disk`, `Initialize-Disk`, `Remove-Partition`, `f

ormat C:` |
| Boot configuration | `bcdedit`, `reg delete HKLM…` |
| Host availability | `Stop-Compu

ter`, `Restart-Computer`, `shutdown /…` |
| Irreversible erase | `cipher /w`, `sdelete` |

Command text is **normalized** before matching (0.4.5): PowerShell's backtick+newline, cmd's
caret+n

ewline and bash's backslash+newline continuations are folded to a space, quotes are
stripped, and al

l whitespace/newlines collapse to a single space. The same action written
differently therefore land

s on the same rule: `shutdown` + newline + `/s`,
`"C:\Windows\System32\shutdown.exe" /s`, and `Start

-Process shutdown -ArgumentList "-s"` all
match "shutdown with a power flag"; `format.com C:` and `r

eg delete HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\…` are
equivalent to `format C:` and `HKLM`. Power flags are matched ag

ainst the real letter set
(`/s` `/r` `/g` `/p` `/h` `/l` `/a`, dashes included), so `Get-Help shutdo

wn -examples` and
[该节后续省略]
#### Why two enforcement layers, not one

`restrict()` masks only the **inherited** tool surface. Its own documentation
(`dsh-tools/lib/index.

js:2985-2987`) says *"Restrictions intersect; scoped registrations
remain visible"*. Meanwhile the o

fficial `dsh-tool-subagent:605-607` registers `subagent`
and `list_subagent_models` directly on the
child's context from `agent/created`.

Measured on a live deployment before this was fixed: a child handed **only `read`** called
`subagent

`, spawned a grandchild, and that grandchild ran with `delegationDepth: 2` and
**97 tools** includin

g `pwsh`, `write`, `edit` and `workflow` — the policy never applied
because the grandchild was not r
egistered by a `delegate` call.
So gate 3 installs both:
| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |

| visible surface | `childCtx.tools.restrict({ allow })` | inherited tools |
| execution surface | a
gent-scoped `childCtx.tools.guard()` | scoped tools that `restrict` cannot see |

The second layer denies any tool outside the allowlist with:
`Tool "subagent" is not in this subagen
t's authorized tool surface (delegate policy); available: read`.
## Compatibility

Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` **0.2.1-rc.2** (0.3.3, 2026-10-29 — gates 1 and 2
checked on a

real `danger-full-access` parent, gate 3 on both a test bench and the same
host). The plugin copies

two small helpers instead of importing sibling `dsh-*` packages,
because a profile's `node_modules`

usually contains only `schemastery` and a static import
would fail at load time. If DSH renames `su

bagentDepth`, `delegationDepth` or the
`sandbox/mode` event, these copies fail **silently** — the pl

ugin tries to `import()` the
official package at runtime and warns when the two disagree, but that c

heck only fires when
the package happens to be resolvable.
